title: Binary formats — where it stands
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: This is the one pilot page that rates a plan, not a product. The binary plane is 607 lines of design and zero shipped code — no classes, no decode engine, no tests, no phase has run. What makes it worth a page is the bet: don't vendor Kaitai, treat a binary file as "a table the bytes forgot to show," decode it in one engine crossing into the `stzTable` analysis stack that already exists — with zero new DLLs. The substrate it stands on is real; everything above it is named, sequenced (BN0–BN5), and unbuilt.
grid_title: Ten lanes — one substrate that ships, nine that are designed
grid_lede: Every lane names what actually exists today, the tools it is fair to measure against, and what the plan of record owes. For a planned plane the "in the engine" column is the honest one: only the byte substrate has code behind it.

lanes.engine: The one real piece: `stzBytes` over an engine handle buffer (`bytes.zig`, 25 `stz_bytes_*` functions) — slice, at, append, replace, plus hex / base64 / binary encoders (`encode.zig`) and `crc32`. Used across the library today.
lanes.owed: Two must-fixes before it can carry a parser: the bridge returns slices through fixed `[4096]`/`[8192]` buffers (silent truncation above those sizes), and there are no typed endian readers — only `byte_swap`.

lanes.engine: Designed: `stzBinarySchema` — pure-Ring nested-list data (never code) naming fields, widths, encodings, repetitions — consumed by a planned `stz_bytes_decode_records` that decodes the whole file in one crossing. No code.
lanes.owed: The heart of the plane. The distinctive choice — a declarative data schema (not a generated parser) decoded by one engine call — is what separates it from Kaitai's compiler model. Owed in full (BN1).

lanes.engine: Planned scalar set `:U8..:U64`, `:I8..:I64`, `:F32`/`:F64`, little- and big-endian. The engine has only `stz_bits_byte_swap` — no `readInt`, no endian-aware scalar decode.
lanes.owed: Typed readers for each width and endianness — the most mechanical part of BN1, and the one every other type depends on.

lanes.engine: UTF-8 is codepoint-correct in the string engine today, but the mainframe encodings the plan targets — `:Ebcdic037`, later CP500 / CP1140 — need 256-byte translation tables that do not exist. Latin-1/ASCII decode is trivial over existing bytes.
lanes.owed: EBCDIC CP037 first (the telco case), then the CP500/CP1140 variants — small, table-driven, and the entry ticket to real mainframe data.

lanes.engine: Planned `:PackedDecimal` (COMP-3) and `:Zoned` (overpunch) decode — the numeric heart of COBOL data. No code, no primitive.
lanes.owed: Nibble-level BCD and overpunch-sign decode. Niche but non-negotiable for the mainframe use case that justifies the plane commercially.

lanes.engine: Planned `stzCopybook` — compile a COBOL copybook into a `stzBinarySchema`. Two fossils exist and the plan disavows both: an empty `max/stzBinaryFile` stub and a lost-2024 telco test calling functions that live nowhere.
lanes.owed: The dialect compiler (BN2), tied to the "RINGBOL" commercial gate and to replaying the telco scene as a guard. The whole lane is owed.

lanes.engine: Planned: flat fields + `:occurs` first, then v2's `:variants` (REDEFINES), RDW variable-length records, and Fortran unformatted framing (`:FortranRecords`). Nothing built.
lanes.owed: The structure grammar beyond flat records — where binary formats get genuinely hard (data-dependent layout). Deliberately staged to v2 (BN4).

lanes.engine: The destination is real: decoded records are meant to land in `stzTable`, where stats, Tukey, plots, CSV/JSON and SQLite already ship. The pipe into it does not exist — nothing decodes yet.
lanes.owed: Once `decode_records` exists, this is a short wire — and it is the payoff: raw bytes become analyzable data in the same stack as every other Softanza source. The distinctive end-state.

lanes.engine: Planned `stzBinaryFileMaker` + `Narrate()` — because a read schema also writes, the same vocabulary runs backwards as an educational surface and a test-fixture factory. No code.
lanes.owed: The reverse engine (`stz_bytes_encode_records`) and the maker face (BN3). A genuine differentiator — most binary parsers cannot round-trip.

lanes.engine: Planned annotated `HexView()`, `DecodeReport()` and `Explore()`, plus batch/streaming with a measured threshold. File I/O today is whole-file only (`stz_file_read` — no seek/chunk).
lanes.owed: The exploration surface (BN4) and a seek/chunk read in `file.zig` before any file too large to hold in memory can be parsed.

gaps_kicker: What to build — the roadmap is the gap list
gaps_title: The phases, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: For a planned plane the gaps are the roadmap (BN0–BN5). Three tiers: the first unblocks everything, the second are the fast wins over an already-real destination, the third is the strategic breadth that justifies the plane commercially.

tiers.title: Tier A — foundational, unblocks the whole plane

items.title: Repair the byte-bridge truncation
items.text: The `[4096]`/`[8192]` fixed return buffers silently truncate any slice above their size — a correctness bug in the one substrate every future lane rests on. It is the literal first step of BN1, and cheap.

items.title: The schema + decode-records engine
items.text: `stzBinarySchema` plus `stz_bytes_decode_records` for scalars, text, packed and zoned — decode the whole file in one crossing into columns. The core of the plane; everything else is either a feeder or a consumer of it.

tiers.title: Tier B — the fast wins over a real destination

items.title: BN0 — the decode-physics spike
items.text: Measurement only: five measurements, six predictions, kill criteria written before the numbers. The plan's own gating first action — proves the "zero new DLLs" bet before a line of product code is written.

items.title: Endian readers + EBCDIC CP037
items.text: Typed little/big-endian scalar readers and the 256-byte CP037 table. Small, table-driven, and together they are the entry ticket to real mainframe records.

items.title: Wire decode into stzTable
items.text: The analysis destination already ships (stats, Tukey, plots, CSV/JSON/SQLite). Once `decode_records` exists, this short wire delivers the whole payoff — bytes become analyzable data in the same stack as every other source.

items.title: COBOL copybook compiler (BN2)
items.text: `stzCopybook` compiling a copybook into a schema, with the lost telco scene replayed as a guard. The commercial gate (tied to "RINGBOL") and the reason mainframe packed/zoned decode is non-negotiable.

items.title: The writer & round-trip (BN3)
items.text: `stz_bytes_encode_records` and `stzBinaryFileMaker` + `Narrate()`. Round-tripping a schema — read and write from one vocabulary — is something most binary parsers cannot do.

items.title: Structure, streaming & the exit decision (BN4–BN5)
items.text: `:occurs`/`:variants`/RDW, Fortran framing, a seek/chunk read for big files — then BN5 decides whether a Kaitai/DFDL-subset importer pays rent, with a standing right to refuse and close the plane.

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings.
notes.text: This page rates a document. `base/binary/` holds exactly one file — the 607-line plan — and its own closing line ("BN RESULTS appended as phases close") sits empty, confirming no phase has run. There is no `test/binary/` directory. Every lane but the byte substrate describes intent; the Partial rating is generous to that substrate, which still needs a truncation repair before it can carry a parser.

Softanza has no binary-format capability today — but it has an unusually disciplined plan and a distinctive architecture: a declarative data schema decoded in one engine crossing into an analysis stack that already exists, built by extending the `stz_bytes` DLL rather than vendoring Kaitai. The bet to watch is whether "zero new DLLs" holds through packed decimal and variable-length records; BN0 is designed to answer that before the plane commits.

footer: Read from the source on 2026-09-16 — `base/binary/` (one file: `SOFTANZA_BINARY_PLAN.md`, 607 lines, 2026-08-16); substrate that ships: `stzBytes` over engine `bytes.zig` / `ring_bridge_bytes.zig`, `string/encode.zig` (hex/base64/binary), `bits.zig` (`byte_swap`), `file.zig` (whole-file read). Fossils disavowed by the plan: `max/stzBinaryFile.ring` stub, `future/stzCobol.ring`. No `test/binary/` exists. Ratings reflect what the guards prove — here, that nothing yet does.
